cells.tense: You are here, in the open moment before anything has to be decided.
cells.act: pick the one you would be sorriest to lose
cells.ask: From what you're holding right now, pick the one you'd miss most if it went, and hold that in view a moment. Leave the rest as they are.
cells.core:
You can stand in front of everything you haven't decided yet and not force any of them into a shape. That's rarer than it sounds. From inside a situation you can still see its whole outline — where you are in it, what it's made of — and you don't use that to judge anyone. You just recognise. People feel known around you without being weighed.

From what you're holding right now, pick the one you'd miss most if it went. Hold it in view a moment. Nothing else moves; the rest can stay exactly as they are. Having one thing quietly leading the others changes how the deciding goes — it stops being a negotiation with everything at once. That's all this is. Just let the first thing be first.
cells.sheetLine: One thing leads the others now, quietly, and the rest can wait.
cells.verb: being everything you could still become, not yet decided
cells.place: a place where you look at the whole shape of what's in front of you from inside it

cells.tense: You will keep every door open, and so none of them will let you through.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Finish something already underway your own way this week — not the polished version. When it's done, don't explain or justify it to anyone.
cells.core:
You can see how every option could still turn out well, so you hold all of them open, and none gets to become anything. Each stays a size larger than the last, softer, so nothing settles into a life that would need living on a schedule. From the inside it feels like staying ready. From outside it reads like nothing has been given the chance to land.

There's another half to this. Finish something already underway the way you alone would finish it. Not the version you'd show someone to prove it. Yours, and no explanation afterward. One piece of work done plainly as itself gives the whole field something to land on. You don't have to settle everything. Just let this one be what it is.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Stay with something you're already carrying, longer than you'd normally stay — past where you'd usually turn away. Notice what it shows you that you didn't have before.
cells.core:
You can usually see the whole shape of a situation from the inside, and a while back that closed. You read from a distance now, aimed at what's already settled. You work from what you know rather than from what's around you. It isn't blindness. It's a shorter leash on looking, and it was probably a sensible one to take.

Stay with something you're already carrying, longer than you'd normally stay. Not a new thing — the same one, seen past where you'd usually turn away. What it shows you will be old ground not yet finished. Nothing has to open today. Looking at the same thing more deeply is how the whole shape comes back.

cells.tense: You are already writing in a room whose doors you cannot see.
cells.act: sketch the whole of it badly, on one page, and keep the sketch
cells.ask: Put something that's been sitting with you onto a single page, roughly — where you are in it, who's with you, what's around. Keep the page when you're done.
cells.core:
You read situations fast, see the whole shape, and move on it before anyone's done explaining. You wouldn't call that seeing. You'd call it reacting, or being practical, or getting along. The recognition is happening; your name isn't on it. So the choices feel like things that happen to you, and the ways through don't look like ways through.

Put something that's been sitting with you onto a single page. Roughly. Where you are in it, who else is in it, what's around it. Keep the page afterward. It doesn't have to be accurate. You want the arrangement you're standing inside to have a line or two you can look at, so the next turn can be told apart from a wall.
cells.sheetLine: You read the room and call it reacting.

attempts.check: The weakest claim is the Balanced ask — that deciding one thing and acting on it same-day is Inspiration's own act; it's the medicine's turn-toward, made small, but a reader could reasonably say it's more about decisiveness than aspiration. The reader's likely objection to the Too Much core is 'I'm not stalling, I'm genuinely exploring,' which is fair — the cell describes the mechanism (possibility kept open past the point of landing) without claiming motive, so even a disagreement leaves the ask usable. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'that's the whole of it' as a cold closer; it's cut. The ask survives a wrong read in every cell: each is small, doable, and teaches the person something about how they want even if the diagnosis is off.
